source.paper: Domain: evolutionary biology / freshwater fish body-size evolution and speciation rates, South America (BAMM/DR diversification analysis).

cases.task: What are the factors most influential in explaining spatial variation in speciation rates?
cases.goldHypothesisText: The rate of maximum body length evolution emerged as the most influential factor explaining spatial variation in speciation rates. The relationship is positive with linear coefficient 0.82.

cases.task: How are evolutionary rates of oral gape position and relative maxillary length related to speciation rates?
cases.goldHypothesisText: Evolutionary rates of oral gape position and relative maxillary length both exhibited a negative relationship with speciation rates. Their respective coefficient of relation is -4.6 and -4.9.

cases.task: Is the rate of body elongation evolution associated with speciation rates?
cases.goldHypothesisText: The rate of body elongation evolution has no significant association with speciation rates.

cases.task: Is species diversity related to speciation rates?
cases.goldHypothesisText: There is a weak but significant, positive relationship between speciation rates and species diversity. The weak relationship is determined by a very small coefficient 0.00003018.
